To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a multimodal gesture-enhancing interface can be designed for information retrieval and presentation; (ii) the interface can be dynamically adapted to user profiles, tasks, and contexts; and (iii) the retrieved information can then be presented in a multimodal and multi-resolution fashion.

we have designed a novel multimodal, gesture-enhanced interface, and that the interface provides immersive as well as natural and non-intrusive interaction between the user, the environment, and the information system.

1) the user can interact with the system by using a gesture-based interface; 2) the system can transform the user's gestures into queries for information retrieval from distributed sources; 3) the system can present the retrieved information in a multi-resolution manner, depending upon the user's location and task; and 4) the user's gestures can be used to navigate in a multi-dimensional space of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a gesture-enhanced interface for a distributed learning environment.
developing a novel multimodal interface for a distributed learning environment which can be used by a large number of students and instructors.
the development of a gesture-based interface to a distributed multimedia information system.
